---
title: "SKI3010 syllabus"
subtitle: "Evidence Synthesis 1: Study Designs in Systematic Reviewing"
---

* Period 4 · 2.5 ECTS · skills training
* Prerequisite: Statistics I (SSC2061); an argued exception is possible. Recommended: Research Methods I (SKI1004), Research Methods II (SKI1005), Presentation Skills (SKI2007).
* Textbook: [*Textbook of Epidemiology*, 2nd edition (Wiley)](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Textbook+of+Epidemiology%2C+2nd+Edition-p-9781119776024), available via the library (KeyLinks).

## This module

SKI3010 lays the foundation. You learn the basic concepts of epidemiology and statistics that every systematic review relies on: study designs, measures of frequency and association, bias and risk of bias, and the logic of meta-analysis. You apply them right away. All groups work on the same review question: does exposure to thimerosal-containing vaccines increase the risk of autism spectrum disorder in children? Starting from the primary studies, you extract study characteristics, assess risk of bias with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, extract quantitative data, perform a meta-analysis first by hand and then in JASP, and write a paper that follows PRISMA 2020. At the end you give individual written feedback on the paper of another group.

## Learning outcomes

After this module you can:

1. explain the basic concepts of systematic reviews, observational study designs and measures of frequency and association;
2. extract study characteristics and assess the risk of bias of observational studies with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale;
3. extract quantitative data and prepare it for meta-analysis;
4. perform and interpret a meta-analysis by hand and in JASP;
5. write a systematic review that follows PRISMA 2020;
6. give constructive feedback on a systematic review written by others.

## Assessment

{{< include _assessment.qmd >}}

The final paper and the peer review are graded with the [rubrics](../rubrics.qmd).

## Rules

* **Groups.** You work in a group of 1 to 3 students and stay in that group for the whole module. Every member is responsible for the whole paper. The peer review is individual.
* **Quizzes.** Paper quiz at the start of the tutorial, no devices. The best 3 of 4 quizzes count. A missed quiz scores 0 and has no separate resit. With documented illness you can take the quiz in the next tutorial.
* **Deadlines.** Hand in via the [submission form](../submit.qmd). The progress assignments A1 to A4 are pass/fail; you get feedback in the next tutorial.
* **Lectures** are optional, their content is not: it is not repeated in the tutorials and is tested in the quiz of the following week. **Tutorials** are where you start your assignment with help from the tutor.
* **AI** is allowed as a tutor; see [AI use](../ai.qmd). Every paper contains a short AI-use paragraph in the methods.
* **Announcements** are sent through Canvas and reach you by e-mail.
